items.followUp: Why is RAM called volatile memory?

rubric.why: Checks that the answer identifies data retention as the defining property.
rubric.description: States that secondary memory retains its stored data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that stored data is retained.

rubric.why: Checks the condition in which non-volatile memory retains data.
rubric.description: States that data remains stored when the computer is switched off or power is interrupted.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that data is retained without power.

modelAnswer: Secondary memory is called non-volatile memory because it retains stored data even when the computer is switched off or the power supply is interrupted.

items.followUp: Draw the truth table for an AND operator.

rubric.why: Checks the output when both inputs are 0.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct 0, 0, 0 row.

rubric.description: Shows that the output is 1 when either or both inputs are 1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when all three remaining rows are correct.

items.followUp: Write the negation of proposition Q and show its truth table.

rubric.why: Checks the notation for the negation of P.
rubric.description: Writes NOT P as ¬P, P′, or NOT P.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct negation notation.

rubric.why: Checks that negation reverses the truth value of P.
rubric.description: Gives both rows of the truth table for P and NOT P.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both truth-table rows are correct.

modelAnswer: NOT P is written as ¬P (or P′).

items.followUp: Define a switch in a computer network.

rubric.why: Checks the router’s role in connecting networks.
rubric.description: States that a router connects two or more networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that it connects networks.

rubric.why: Checks how a router directs network traffic.
rubric.description: States that it forwards data packets between networks, typically using IP addresses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing packet forwarding or IP-based routing.

modelAnswer: A router is a networking device that connects two or more networks and forwards data packets between them, using IP addresses to direct the packets.
